recognize_zh: 臨床照片中，年輕女性的額頭、雙眼淚管、鼻孔、肚臍與手指皮膚表面有血液滲出，但皮膚沒有明顯傷口、瘀斑或紫斑，這種完整皮膚自發性滲血符合血汗症（hematidrosis）。
features: Clinical photographs of a young woman with fresh blood streaks on the forehead running down the nasal bridge
Bloody tears flowing from both medial canthi (hemolacria) and blood below the nostrils and on the upper lip
Blood oozing from the umbilicus and from the dorsal skin of a finger
No visible laceration, ecchymosis, petechiae or purpura on the bleeding skin surfaces
Non-morphologic image; diagnosis relies on clinical exclusion of coagulopathy and factitious bleeding
describe_en: Clinical photographs show an 18-year-old woman with spontaneous bleeding from intact skin and mucosa: blood streaks on the central forehead, bloody tears from both lacrimal regions, blood below the nares, oozing from the umbilicus and a bleeding spot on the dorsum of a finger. The skin surrounding these sites shows no visible wound, bruising or petechial rash. This is not a histologic or cytologic image; interpretation requires normal platelet counts, platelet function and coagulation studies and exclusion of self-inflicted bleeding. Findings are consistent with hematidrosis (hematohidrosis).

ddx.vs: Factitious disorder shows traumatic lesions or bleeding only when unobserved, whereas hematidrosis episodes can be witnessed arising from intact skin with blood cells in sweat on microscopy.

ddx.dx: Inherited or acquired bleeding disorder (VWD, platelet function defect, coagulopathy)
ddx.vs: True bleeding disorders produce abnormal coagulation or platelet function tests and typically ecchymoses or mucosal bleeding at sites of trauma, not blood from intact forehead or navel skin.
Colored sweat from lipofuscin or chromogenic bacteria lacks red blood cells on microscopic examination and is occult-blood negative.

ddx.dx: Hemolacria from local ocular or nasal pathology
ddx.vs: Local conjunctival or nasolacrimal lesions cause isolated bloody tears, not simultaneous bleeding from multiple distant skin sites.
